sourcedFrom: Safety & Instruction Manual ENCORE® Rifle & Shotgun Including ENCORE® PROHunter™ Models — Copyright © 2024 Thompson/Center Arms (2024)
cleanIntro: Thompson/Center's own cleaning procedure for the Encore rifle and shotgun, from the one book T/C prints for both, PROHunter models included (the pistol and muzzleloader Encores have books of their own). The Encore is a single-shot break-action: pulling up and back on the trigger guard spur unlocks the barrel and it tips down at the muzzle. The routine strip is the forend off and the barrel off the frame by its hinge pin, and the book says that is as far as an owner takes the gun.

steps.title: Hammer at rest, pull the trigger guard spur, barrel tips down
steps.action: Muzzle in a safe direction, finger away from the trigger and the hammer in the At Rest position, pull up and back on the trigger guard spur. The barrel unlocks and tips down, exposing the chamber.
steps.prose: On the Encore the trigger guard is the action release: it moves up and back to open the gun. T/C's tip is to put your finger low on the spur for leverage and give it a fast, sharp pull. Open the action every time you pick the gun up, before anything else happens.
steps.quote: With your finger away from the trigger and with the hammer in the “AT REST” position (FIGURE 7), open the action by pulling up and back on the trigger guard spur (FIGURE 9).
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual ENCORE® Rifle & Shotgun Including ENCORE® PROHunter™ Models — Copyright © 2024 Thompson/Center Arms — INSPECTING, p.13
steps.warn: ANY TIME THAT YOU HANDLE AN ENCORE®, OPEN THE ACTION AND ENSURE THAT IT IS UNLOADED.

steps.title: Take the cartridge or shell out of the chamber
steps.action: With the hammer still at rest and the action open, remove any cartridge or shell from the chamber by hand.
steps.prose: The Encore is a single shot, so the chamber is the only place a round can be. Take it out and set it away from the bench before you go on.
steps.quote: With the hammer in the “At Rest” position, open the action and remove the cartridge from the chamber (FIGURES 28 & 29).
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual ENCORE® Rifle & Shotgun Including ENCORE® PROHunter™ Models — Copyright © 2024 Thompson/Center Arms — UNLOADING, p.21

steps.title: Look into the chamber and through the bore
steps.action: Look into the barrel from the breech end and confirm there is no shell in the chamber, then confirm the bore is clear and free of obstructions.
steps.prose: With the barrel tipped down you can see straight down the bore from the breech. T/C asks for this check every time the gun leaves your hand, is cleaned, handed over, transported or stored.
steps.quote: Look into the barrel from the breech end to make sure there is no shell in the chamber (FIGURE 8). Verify that the bore is clear and free of obstructions.
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual ENCORE® Rifle & Shotgun Including ENCORE® PROHunter™ Models — Copyright © 2024 Thompson/Center Arms — INSPECTING, p.13

steps.title: Confirm the chamber empty, then close the action
steps.action: With the hammer at rest, open the action once more, make sure the chamber is empty, then close the action.
steps.prose: T/C's takedown starts with the gun closed: the forend screws come out with the barrel shut on the frame.
steps.quote: With the hammer in the “At Rest” position, open the action and make sure that the chamber is empty - then close the action.
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual ENCORE® Rifle & Shotgun Including ENCORE® PROHunter™ Models — Copyright © 2024 Thompson/Center Arms — TAKEDOWN OF THE ENCORE RIFLE OR SHOTGUN, p.26

steps.title: Forend screws out, forend off
steps.action: Turn the forend screw or screws out counterclockwise, as viewed from the bottom of the gun, and take the forend off the barrel.
steps.prose: Depending on the barrel there may be one forend screw or more. Keep them together: the same screws go back in to hold the forend on. Rifle, shotgun and muzzleloading barrels each take their own forend.
steps.quote: Remove the forend screw(s). Turn these screws out counterclockwise (as viewed from the bottom of the gun). Remove the forend from the barrel.
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual ENCORE® Rifle & Shotgun Including ENCORE® PROHunter™ Models — Copyright © 2024 Thompson/Center Arms — TAKEDOWN OF THE ENCORE RIFLE OR SHOTGUN, p.26

steps.title: Open the action, tap out the hinge pin, barrel off
steps.action: Open the action to take the tension off the hinge pin, tap the hinge pin out in either direction, and lift the barrel off the frame.
steps.prose: The hinge pin is what anchors the barrel lug to the frame, and with the action open it is no longer under load. It comes out either way. With the barrel off, the frame, stock and barrel are the three groups the book names.
steps.quote: Open the action to remove the tension on the hinge pin and remove the hinge pin by tapping it out (in either direction). Remove the barrel from the frame.
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual ENCORE® Rifle & Shotgun Including ENCORE® PROHunter™ Models — Copyright © 2024 Thompson/Center Arms — TAKEDOWN OF THE ENCORE RIFLE OR SHOTGUN, p.26

steps.title: Stop here: this is the owner's limit
steps.action: Go no further. Barrel off the frame is as far as T/C has an owner take the Encore apart, for routine maintenance and for swapping stocks, barrels and forends.
steps.prose: The hammer, sear and firing pin live inside the frame, and the book publishes no procedure for them. Anything beyond this point goes to Thompson/Center Customer Service.
steps.quote: This diagram shows the extent to which the ENCORE® should be disassembled by the user for routine maintenance and interchange of accessory stocks, barrels and forends (FIGURE 31).
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual ENCORE® Rifle & Shotgun Including ENCORE® PROHunter™ Models — Copyright © 2024 Thompson/Center Arms — TAKEDOWN OF THE ENCORE RIFLE OR SHOTGUN, p.26
steps.warn: NEVER DISASSEMBLE YOUR FIREARM BEYOND THE PROCEDURES OUTLINED IN THIS MANUAL. IMPROPER DISASSEMBLY OR REASSEMBLY OF YOUR FIREARM MAY BE DANGEROUS AND CAN LEAD TO SERIOUS INJURY OR DEATH.

steps.title: Brass brush and solvent through the bore and chamber
steps.action: Scrub the firing residue out of the bore and the chamber with a properly fitted brass brush dipped in gun cleaning solvent.
steps.prose: A properly fitted brush is one made for your bore, and the Encore takes barrels in many calibers and gauges, so match the brush to the barrel in front of you. Use a solvent made for firearms.
steps.quote: Remove excessive firing residue from the bore and chamber using a properly fitted brass brush dipped in gun cleaning solvent.
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual ENCORE® Rifle & Shotgun Including ENCORE® PROHunter™ Models — Copyright © 2024 Thompson/Center Arms — CLEANING AND MAINTENANCE, p.23
steps.warn: Ammoniated solvents or other strong alkaline solvents, should not be used on any Thompson/Center firearm.

steps.title: Dry patch to finish the bore
steps.action: Finish by running a dry cotton patch through the bore to lift out the loosened residue and the solvent.
steps.prose: The dry patch is the last thing through the bore in T/C's procedure. Solvent left in the bore is not lubrication.
steps.quote: Finish the bore cleaning process by running a dry cotton cloth patch through the bore to remove residue and solvent.
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual ENCORE® Rifle & Shotgun Including ENCORE® PROHunter™ Models — Copyright © 2024 Thompson/Center Arms — CLEANING AND MAINTENANCE, p.23

steps.title: Wipe the outside, then a light coat of oil on the metal
steps.action: Clean the outside of the gun with a non-abrasive cloth, then put a light coat of good firearm oil on the metal parts, inside and out.
steps.prose: Inside and out includes the frame and the barrel lug where the hinge pin runs, which are easy to reach with the barrel off.
steps.quote: Clean the exterior of the firearm using a non-abrasive cleaning cloth. After cleaning, lightly coat the metal parts, internal and external with a high quality firearm oil.
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual ENCORE® Rifle & Shotgun Including ENCORE® PROHunter™ Models — Copyright © 2024 Thompson/Center Arms — CLEANING AND MAINTENANCE, p.23

steps.title: Take the fingerprints off
steps.action: Wipe any cleaning solution, oil and fingerprints off the outside surfaces of the gun.
steps.prose: T/C's reason is corrosion: moisture from your fingers left on the steel can start rust.
steps.quote: Remove any gun cleaning solution, oil and fingerprints from the outside surfaces of the firearm. (Finger moisture, if left, could start a corrosion process.)
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual ENCORE® Rifle & Shotgun Including ENCORE® PROHunter™ Models — Copyright © 2024 Thompson/Center Arms — CLEANING AND MAINTENANCE, p.24

steps.title: Shotgun barrels: clean and lightly lube the choke tube threads
steps.action: On a shotgun barrel with screw-in chokes, take the choke tube out with the T/C choke wrench (counterclockwise removes it) and clean the threads on the tube and in the barrel. Keep them lightly lubricated with an anti-seize lubricant.
steps.prose: Rifle barrels skip this screen. Clogged threads are why a tube will not screw in easily, and a tube forced in can cross-thread. Only T/C tubes go in a T/C shotgun.
steps.quote: The threads of your T/C® choke tubes should be kept clean and lightly lubricated at all times
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual ENCORE® Rifle & Shotgun Including ENCORE® PROHunter™ Models — Copyright © 2024 Thompson/Center Arms — INSTALLATION OF CHOKE TUBES IN ENCORE SHOTGUNS, p.29
steps.warn: Never fire your ENCORE® shotgun, which has been designed to accept internal choke tubes, WITHOUT A CHOKE TUBE INSTALLED.

steps.title: Check for wear every time you clean
steps.action: Look the gun over for signs of wear each time you clean it. If you find wear, do not use the gun: return it to Thompson/Center for service or have a qualified gunsmith check it.
steps.prose: The same goes for the stock: T/C says that if you ever see cracking in the stock at or near the stock bolt, stop using that stock and send it back to Thompson/Center for inspection.
steps.quote: Every time you clean your firearm, check it for signs of wear. If wear is noted, do not use the firearm. Return it to Thompson/Center for service or have it checked by a qualified gunsmith.
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual ENCORE® Rifle & Shotgun Including ENCORE® PROHunter™ Models — Copyright © 2024 Thompson/Center Arms — MAINTENANCE BEFORE STORAGE, p.24

deepAbsentReason: There is no deep clean for the Encore rifle and shotgun, and this guide does not invent one. Thompson/Center's book ends the owner's disassembly at the takedown (forend off, hinge pin out, barrel off the frame) and states on page 26 that this is the extent to which the Encore should be disassembled by the user for routine maintenance. On page 23 it says never to disassemble the firearm beyond its field stripping and inspection sections. The hammer, sear and firing pin inside the frame are not for the bench; other service goes to Thompson/Center Customer Service.

cleaning.name: BORE & CHAMBER
tasks: Properly fitted brass brush dipped in firearm solvent through the bore and chamber
Dry cotton patch through the bore to finish
Do not use ammoniated or strong alkaline solvents on a Thompson/Center firearm

cleaning.name: METAL & EXTERIOR
tasks: Wipe the outside with a non-abrasive cloth
Light coat of firearm oil on the metal parts, inside and out
Wipe off cleaning solution, oil and fingerprints
For long storage, oil the bore, chamber and internal surfaces

cleaning.name: CHOKE TUBE (SHOTGUN BARRELS)
tasks: Choke tube out with the T/C wrench, counterclockwise
Clean the tube and barrel threads; keep them lightly lubricated with anti-seize
Never fire a choke-tube barrel without a tube installed

reassembly: Before assembly, put a light film of quality firearm oil on all the metal parts.
The forend must be off the barrel before the barrel goes on the frame. Insert the barrel lug into the frame.
Line up the hinge pin holes in the barrel and the frame and insert the hinge pin. Centre it so it does not stick out of either side, then tip the barrel up and closed on the frame.
Place the rear of the forend against the receiver, line up the holes in the forend over the holes in the barrel, and secure it with the supplied forend screws.

Shotgun barrels: refit the choke tube clockwise. It should screw in easily by hand; if it does not, the threads may be clogged or crossed, so do not force it. Snug it with the wrench and do not over-tighten it.

If you changed the stock: use the factory stock bolt and washer, and tighten the bolt clockwise to 50 inch-pounds (plus or minus 5) with a torque driver and a 3/16-inch socket head. Over-tightening can compress the stock and crack it at the grip.
fncheck: With the gun unloaded, check that the hammer and trigger work properly before you load and fire it. T/C requires this check after reassembly but prints no step-by-step test for it. Open and close the action with the trigger guard spur and confirm the barrel locks up closed. If you dry-fire to check the hammer, use a snap cap of the right cartridge designation, as T/C directs, so the firing pin is not damaged. If the gun feels or sounds different from normal, do not fire it: contact Thompson/Center Customer Service.
breakOpen: pull up and back on the trigger guard spur and let the barrel tip down.
